title: Bigger MAX_ITER on top candidates only
spec: Keep MAX_ITER=200 for restarts, and store the top 3 raw (unrepaired) results. In the final 15% of the time, rerun SLSQP from each with maxiter 1000 and ftol 1e-12, then repair and keep the best. Raw results must be stored before repair.

title: Multiprocess-free time slicing by early abort on stalled SLSQP
spec: Run SLSQP with a callback that raises StopIteration-style exit (catch a custom exception) when the radius sum after 80 iterations is below 90 percent of the best known final sum. Catch the exception and skip that restart. Use the last iterate only if it was not aborted. This stops hopeless runs cheaply while allowing the good ones to run to MAX_ITER 300.

title: Swap small and large circle positions
spec: After the restart phase, loop on the best solution. Pick two circles with different radii at random and swap their centres. Set radii to the mean radius for both, then re-optimize with SLSQP (maxiter 100). Repair and accept if the sum improves. This explores permutations of the size assignment that SLSQP cannot reach by itself.

title: Two-phase SLSQP with radius target
spec: Phase 1: run SLSQP for 60 iterations with all radii tied to a single shared value via the objective -sum r plus the constraint set, using start radius 0.05. Phase 2: continue from the result with free radii for the remaining iterations (up to MAX_ITER 200). Use the hex init. This gives an equal-circle-like start before breaking size symmetry.

title: Mixed-size hex init
spec: In _solve_once, build the start from a hex grid with 5-6 rows as now. Choose about 4 random circles to be big, and set their initial radii to 0.12 and all other radii to 0.07. Put the big circles near random grid points. Known good packings of this kind have a few large circles among smaller ones, so this should favor those. Keep everything else the same.

title: Mixed-size hex init with a few large circles
spec: In the init, pick 4 to 6 random points and set their initial radius to 0.11 while the rest start at 0.05. Remove neighbours of those points that lie closer than 0.12 and refill the count from the remaining grid points. Best known packings of this problem contain a few larger circles, so this seeds that structure.

title: Sort-and-move the worst circle
spec: Identify the circle with the smallest radius in the best solution, and move it to a random location with radius 0.01 while shrinking the neighbours that overlap it. Re-run SLSQP for 100 iterations. Repeat for each of the 5 smallest circles in turn.

title: Analytic gradient and Jacobian plus hex init with MAX_ITER 300
spec: Supply jac for the objective (-1 on radii, 0 on centres) and a dense analytic Jacobian for cons (pair rows: derivative of distance wrt both centres and -1 for both radii; wall rows; identity for r>=0). Raise MAX_ITER to 300 so each SLSQP converges further. Keep the hex init and the 0.8 time fraction.

title: Mirror-symmetric init
spec: With probability 0.5 per restart, build the starting centres by generating 16 random hex-jittered points in the left half (x<0.5) and mirroring them to x -> 1-x to make 32. Do not impose symmetry on the optimizer. SLSQP will then break it when that is favourable. Symmetric starts often lead to good packings.

title: Pre-relax with L-BFGS-B on hex init, 30 steps
spec: Before SLSQP in _solve_once, run scipy L-BFGS-B for 30 iterations on the centres only (radii fixed at INIT_RADIUS) to minimise the sum of squared pair overlaps plus squared wall violations, using an analytic gradient. Then start SLSQP from the relaxed centres. This repeats slot 19 (-2.9396), which was within noise, so run it again to see if it is real.

title: Elite crossover of halves
spec: Keep top 6 distinct repaired packings from the first 60% of time. In the remaining time create children: pick two parents, take circles of parent A with x<t (t random in 0.35..0.65) and circles of parent B with x>=t, adjusting to exactly n by dropping or adding random-position circles with small radii. Run SLSQP maxiter 200 from the child, and add the result to the elite pool if good.

title: Mirror-symmetric init
spec: With probability 0.5 per restart, generate 16 jittered hex-grid points in the left half (x<0.5) and mirror them across x=0.5 to get 32 centres, with the initial radii copied from the mirrored partner. SLSQP then runs unconstrained by symmetry so it can break it.

title: Analytic Jacobian plus hex-grid init, MAX_ITER 300
spec: Add an analytic objective gradient (-1 on radii entries) and a dense analytic constraint Jacobian for the pair, wall and r>=0 constraints in _solve_once, passed via jac= in minimize. Raise MAX_ITER to 300 so that each SLSQP run converges more fully. Keep TIME_FRACTION and the init unchanged. This combines slot 6 (-2.9396) with the incumbent init and gives deeper convergence per run.

title: Exact LP radius repair
spec: Replace _repair with a linear program: keep centres fixed and solve for radii maximizing sum(r) subject to r_i + r_j <= d_ij for all pairs, r_i <= distance to walls, r >= 0, using scipy.optimize.linprog (highs). Then subtract SHRINK (1e-9) and run the existing pairwise check, shrinking any remaining violating pair so the result stays valid. Apply it to every restart result and to the final best. This recovers the radius sum lost by the greedy shrinking.

title: Final best-packing polish by alternating LP and active-set solve
spec: After the restart loop ends at 80 percent of the time, spend the rest on the best packing. Repeat: fix the centres and solve the exact radius LP with linprog (HiGHS). Then run SLSQP with only the near-active pairs (gap under 0.02) and walls, started from the LP radii, with ftol 1e-14. Stop when the gain is under 1e-9. Keep the result only if the repaired sum is greater.

title: Final tight polish of the best packing
spec: Reserve the last 10% of time (restarts stop at 0.7 of the limit). Take the best packing before repair and run SLSQP from it with maxiter 1000 and ftol 1e-14, then repair. Keep the result only if the repaired sum is larger.

title: Squared-distance constraints with analytic Jacobian
spec: Rewrite the pair constraints in SLSQP as (dx^2+dy^2) - (ri+rj)^2 >= 0, which is smooth at zero distance. Supply an analytic dense Jacobian for all constraints. Keep MAX_ITER 200 and the hex init. The repair step still guarantees validity. Test whether the smoother constraints give better local optima.

title: Replicate baseline with analytic Jacobian and MAX_ITER 400
spec: Keep the hex-grid init. Add an analytic objective gradient (-1 on radii) and a dense analytic constraint Jacobian for the pair, wall and radius constraints, and pass jac to SLSQP. Raise MAX_ITER to 400 so that each run converges fully. Keep TIME_FRACTION 0.8 and the existing repair. This combines the two slots that looked slightly positive (6 and the long-iteration idea).

title: Batch of cheap runs with the best 10% continued in parallel pool
spec: For the first 50% of the time, run each restart for only 40 SLSQP iterations and store the raw state with its objective. Then sort the states and continue only the top 8 for 300 iterations each, with the analytic Jacobian. This is a successive-halving schedule that differs from slot 17 by using the Jacobian and a fixed top-8 budget instead of a percentage.

title: Two-size hex init
spec: Make the init with mixed sizes. Pick 4 to 8 random points and give them initial radius 0.11. Give the others 0.05. Use the jittered hex centres but move each big point away from its nearest neighbours by 0.03. Run SLSQP unchanged.

title: Final-phase scaled-variable SLSQP polish
spec: After restarts (use 85% of time), take the best raw SLSQP solution and re-run SLSQP with the analytic Jacobian, maxiter 500 and ftol 1e-15, with variables rescaled so that radii are multiplied by 10. Then run the repair. Only accept the result if the repaired sum improves.

title: Squared-distance constraints with Jacobian
spec: Change the pair constraints to (dx^2+dy^2) - (ri+rj)^2 >= 0, which is smooth at zero distance. Provide the analytic sparse-free Jacobian over the pair index arrays via jac=. Use it in SLSQP, and keep the wall and r>=0 constraints linear. The cheaper, smoother evaluations should allow more restarts in the same time.

title: Two-size hex init
spec: Start with 3-5 randomly chosen circles at initial radius 0.10 and the rest at 0.055. Place the large ones at hex-grid points with the same jitter. Optimal packings of this problem have mixed radii, so this puts diversity in the starts. This differs from slot 43, because the large circles sit on lattice points rather than at random positions.

title: Large-circle-count hex lattice with deletion of smallest-gap points
spec: Build a hex lattice with n+3 to n+6 points (random rows 5-7). Jitter them, then drop the points that have the smallest nearest-neighbour distance until n remain. This gives better-balanced starts than a random subset. The rest of the pipeline is unchanged.

title: Perturb-and-reoptimise radii-only kick on best
spec: In the last 25% of the time, take the best packing, multiply each radius by a random factor in [0.6, 1.0] and add centre noise of sd 0.005 to only the 5 circles with smallest radii, then run SLSQP from there with MAX_ITER 200. Accept if the repaired sum improves. This is a small local kick aimed at the weakest circles, unlike the earlier global basin hops.

title: Weighted objective warm-up
spec: Run the first 40 SLSQP iterations with the objective -sum(r**0.7). This favours equal radii and so avoids early collapse of circles. Then continue SLSQP with the true linear objective from that state for up to 160 iterations. Keep the hex init.

title: Squared-distance constraints with Jacobian
spec: Reformulate the pair constraints as (dx^2+dy^2) - (ri+rj)^2 >= 0, which is smooth at zero distance and cheap, and give an analytic Jacobian. Keep the wall constraints. Keep everything else the same. The smoother constraints may let SLSQP converge in fewer iterations and allow more restarts in the time budget.

title: Squared-distance constraints with Jacobian
spec: Replace the pair constraint sqrt(d2)-ri-rj>=0 by a smooth form: d2-(ri+rj)^2>=0 with analytic Jacobian (2*(ci-cj) for centres, -2*(ri+rj) for radii). Avoids the sqrt singularity and speeds up SLSQP, allowing more restarts. Keep the final _repair for exactness.

title: Analytic gradient+Jacobian with 30-step L-BFGS-B pre-relax combined
spec: Add an analytic objective gradient and dense analytic constraint Jacobian to SLSQP (pair, wall rows, and r>=0 rows). Before SLSQP, relax the hex-grid centres with 30 L-BFGS-B iterations on a squared-overlap penalty with fixed radius INIT_RADIUS. Keep MAX_ITER 200 and the 80 percent time fraction. Both changes gave -2.9396 alone, so test them together.

title: Bandit over row count R
spec: Track the best repaired radius sum for each R in {5,6,7}. For the first 30 percent of the time, cycle R. Afterwards pick R with probability proportional to softmax(mean of the best 2 sums per R divided by 0.005). Everything else stays the same.

title: Replicate slot 0 with analytic gradient+Jacobian and pre-relax combined
spec: Combine the analytic objective gradient and dense constraint Jacobian for SLSQP (as in slot 6) with 30 steps of L-BFGS-B overlap-penalty pre-relaxation of the hex-grid centres (as in slot 19) before SLSQP. Keep MAX_ITER 200 and TIME_FRACTION 0.8. This tests whether the repeated -2.9396 results stack.

title: Corner-pinned init
spec: Place 4 circles at the square's corners at radius 0.09, then fill the remaining 28 from the jittered hex grid with points that lie closer than 0.1 to a corner removed. Run SLSQP as usual. Optimal packings often have large corner circles.

title: Remove and reinsert the worst circles into holes
spec: After 60% of the time, for the best packing: remove the 2 smallest circles. Find the point with maximal clearance among 4000 random samples (distance to the nearest remaining circle edge and the walls). Place the removed circles there with initial radius equal to the clearance, then run SLSQP with MAX_ITER 200 from this state. Keep the result if it is better. Repeat until the time is used.

title: Remove and reinsert smallest circle in largest hole
spec: After 70% of the time, take the best packing, delete the smallest circle, estimate the largest hole by evaluating a 60x60 grid of points for max distance-to-nearest-surface (distance to circles minus radius, and wall distance), place the circle there with radius half that value, then run SLSQP maxiter 150. Repeat with the 2nd and 3rd smallest circles too. Accept improvements only.

title: Two-size hex init with n-k big circles at lattice sites
spec: Use a lattice of about 25 sites with initial radius 0.065 and add 7 extra small circles (radius 0.03) at random lattice interstices (midpoints of three neighbouring sites). Jitter all by sd 0.015. Best published packings contain mixed sizes, so this targets that structure.

title: Square-lattice plus shift init variants
spec: With probability 0.3 per restart, build the init from a 6x6 square grid with 32 points chosen at random. Shift alternate rows by a random fraction of the cell width and add jitter sd 0.02. Otherwise use the hex init. This adds structural diversity of a different kind than the earlier mirror and half-grid starts.

title: Independent-run budget by CPU slicing with best-of-k final long run
spec: Spend 60% of the time on restarts with MAX_ITER=100 and store raw results. Take the best 2 and continue SLSQP from each with MAX_ITER=600 and ftol=1e-12 using analytic Jacobian. Repair and return the best. This differs from earlier polishes by working on top-2 with a much higher iteration cap.

title: Objective smoothing: sum of radii minus small overlap-slack homotopy
spec: Run SLSQP first with constraints relaxed by a slack eps=0.02 (pair distance >= r_i+r_j-eps, walls likewise), 60 iterations, then rerun from that result with eps=0 for the remaining iterations. This lets circles overlap early and untangle later, a different homotopy from earlier gap-based attempts.

title: Analytic gradient/Jacobian with many more restarts per time
spec: Provide analytic objective gradient (-1 on radii) and a dense constraint Jacobian for the pair, wall and r>=0 constraints (pair rows: d/dc_i=(ci-cj)/dist, d/dr=-1). Set MAX_ITER=150 and keep the hex init. Nothing else changes. The aim is simply to run about 2x more restarts in the same CPU time.

title: Jacobian plus top-K long polish
spec: Use the analytic Jacobian. Run restarts with MAX_ITER=100 for 70% of the time and keep the top 4 raw solutions. For the remaining time, continue SLSQP from each of them with maxiter 500 and ftol 1e-12. Repair and return the best result.

title: Batch of short runs, then Jacobian-polished top 5
spec: Using the analytic Jacobian, run MAX_ITER=60 starts for 55% of the time. Keep the 5 best by radius sum, after a quick repair. Continue each with SLSQP for 400 more iterations in the remaining time. Choose the best final packing.

title: Analytic gradient and Jacobian, plain
spec: Give SLSQP an analytic objective gradient (-1 on the radius entries, 0 elsewhere) and a dense analytic constraint Jacobian. Cover the pair, wall and r>=0 constraints. Keep MAX_ITER=200 and the hex init. Runs get faster, so more restarts fit in the time. Slots 6, 44, 47, 50 and 65 gave -2.9396. This is meant as a clean replicate to confirm the gain.

title: Variable scaling and tighter ftol SLSQP
spec: Pass options ftol=1e-10 and use MAX_ITER 400, but terminate restarts early with a callback if the objective improved by less than 1e-6 over the last 20 iterations. This lets good runs converge fully while stalled ones free up time.

title: Remove-k and regrow via radius LP
spec: For the last 30% of the time, take the best packing. Delete 2-4 random circles, which includes some of the small ones. Reinsert them at random points. Then run SLSQP with all radii started at 0.8 of their current values. Accept the result only if it improves. This differs from the earlier moves because the radii are reset and several circles are re-seeded at once.

title: Exact LP radius repair after SLSQP
spec: Replace _repair with: clip centres to [0,1], then solve the linear program max sum r subject to r_i + r_j <= d_ij, r_i <= distance to walls, r>=0 using scipy.optimize.linprog (highs). Then subtract SHRINK 1e-10 from the radii and clip at 0. This recovers radius lost by the greedy shrinking. Verify validity by a final pairwise check; if any pair violates, fall back to the old repair.

title: Alternating LP and centre-gradient polish of best
spec: After the restarts end (use the last 25% of the time), take the best packing. Loop: solve the radius LP for fixed centres with linprog. Then move centres a small step along the LP dual-weighted gradient of the active constraints, or run SLSQP from the current point with MAX_ITER 300 and tight ftol=1e-15. Keep the result only if the repaired sum improves. This pushes the best basin to its exact local optimum.

title: Multi-start with square-lattice-plus-shift variants
spec: With probability 0.3 per restart, use a jittered square-grid init instead of the hex grid. Use 6x6 points with 4 removed at random and a random row shift. Hex is used for the rest. This tests a different structural basin family.

title: Hex init with anisotropic stretch and random phase
spec: Generate the hex lattice with a random x-scale in [0.9, 1.1] and a random column phase offset per row. Choose the row count R from 5 to 7. Then drop random points down to n and jitter with sd 0.02. The aim is to diversify the lattice defects without changing the overall structure.

title: Hex init with random lattice phase and anisotropic scaling
spec: Generate a staggered lattice with R rows and m columns, then apply a random x-scale in [0.9,1.1] about the centre and a random row-phase shift of the stagger (0 to 1 cell). Take n points nearest the square's centre after clipping and jitter by sd 0.02. This broadens the lattice-like basins without changing the optimizer.

title: Bigger batch: half-length runs, double restarts, then polish top 5
spec: Use MAX_ITER 100 for 65 percent of the time, keeping the raw results of the top 5 by radius sum. For the remaining time, continue each of those 5 raw solutions with SLSQP for 300 more iterations from its own state, and then repair and return the best. This differs from earlier screening ideas by continuing the raw solutions rather than restarting them.

title: Batched two-phase: half restarts then top-5 long continuation
spec: For 55% of the time, run SLSQP restarts with MAX_ITER=80 and keep the raw results. Take the top 5 by raw radius sum. Continue each with SLSQP at maxiter 500 and ftol 1e-12, splitting the remaining time evenly. Repair and return the best. Cap each continuation by a time check via a callback that raises StopIteration-like exit.

title: Analytic Jacobian with parallel-free many restarts, MAX_ITER 150
spec: Add an analytic objective gradient and a dense analytic constraint Jacobian (pair, wall, and radius-nonnegativity rows) to SLSQP. Set MAX_ITER=150 and TIME_FRACTION=0.9. The faster iterations should give about 3x more restarts. Keep the rest of the file unchanged.

title: Hex init with larger stagger shift and random column phase
spec: In the hex init, replace the fixed 0.5 row stagger with a random shift s in [0.3,0.7] per restart. Add a random global x phase in [0,1/(m+0.5)] with wraparound mod 1 before the clipping. Keep the jitter sd at 0.02.

title: Penalty-free growth continuation on radii bounds
spec: Run SLSQP three times per restart, with an upper bound on every radius of 0.07, then 0.10, then 0.2, each warm-started from the previous result with 70 iterations. The bound is supplied as an additional inequality constraint. This is a continuation scheme that lets the circles grow gradually and avoids early tangles.

title: Mirror-symmetric init
spec: In _solve_once, with probability 0.5 build the start from n//2 jittered hex-grid points in the left half (x<0.5), mirror them across x=0.5, and add a centre-line circle if n is odd. Otherwise use the normal init. SLSQP runs on all variables and may break the symmetry. Draw the half-points by the same staggered grid restricted to x<0.5.

title: Squared-distance constraints with Jacobian
spec: Reformulate the SLSQP pair constraints as (dx^2+dy^2) - (r_i+r_j)^2 >= 0 with an analytic sparse-free dense Jacobian, also add r_i+r_j >= 0 implicit via r>=0. This removes the sqrt singularity and speeds each iteration, permitting more restarts. Final validity is still guaranteed by the repair step.

title: Increase MAX_ITER to 500 with Jacobian
spec: Raise MAX_ITER from 200 to 500 and add ftol=1e-10 so that SLSQP converges fully to a local optimum rather than stopping early. Use together with analytic gradients if present.

title: Corner-aware init: pin 4 circles in corners
spec: Start four randomly chosen circles at the four corner positions (r, r) with r=0.09. Place the other n-4 on the jittered hex grid, with grid points within 0.1 of the corners removed. Best known packings put larger circles in the corners.

title: Analytic Jacobian plus gradient, replicated with the hex init and no other changes
spec: Add jac=lambda v: gradient of -sum(r) (zeros for centres, -1 for radii) and a dense analytic constraint Jacobian to the SLSQP call, keeping MAX_ITER=200 and everything else as is. Pair rows: d/dc_i=(ci-cj)/dist, d/dc_j=-(ci-cj)/dist, d/dr_i=d/dr_j=-1. Wall rows: the obvious unit entries. The r>=0 rows: identity on the radii. Guard dist with a 1e-12 floor. This is the most consistent small gain seen (-2.9396 seven times), so confirming it gives a cleaner base.

title: Squared-distance constraints with Jacobian in a looser form
spec: Replace the sqrt pair constraints with (dx^2+dy^2) - (ri+rj)^2 >= 0, provide the analytic dense Jacobian, and also give the objective gradient. Keep MAX_ITER 200. The aim is smoother constraints and faster iterations, hence more restarts in the same time.

title: Replicate-safe seed-offset check of baseline
spec: Make no algorithmic change except to derive rng from np.random.default_rng(seed + 1000). This estimates how much of the -2.9375 incumbent is seed luck. Use it as a baseline for later comparisons.

title: Remove-and-regrow via random hole insertion with SLSQP
spec: In the last 30% of the time, take the best packing. Pick k=1 to 3 random circles, delete them, and place each at a random point of a sampled grid of 2000 points, choosing the point with the largest clearance (distance to the nearest centre minus its radius, and to the walls). Set each new circle's radius to 0.5 of the clearance. Run SLSQP with MAX_ITER 150 from there. Keep the result if its repaired sum is better.
